D1.rationale: The order of the two PEEP strategies was generated by computer and allocated centrally by telephone, and the observed sequence allocation was balanced (16 vs 14), with no baseline imbalance reported. The signalling questions give 1.1 Y, 1.2 Y, 1.3 N, so both the tool's algorithm and my judgement are Low.

DS.rationale: S.1 Y (sequences nearly equal, 16 vs 14, so any general trend over time cancels); S.2 is NA because its condition was not met; S.3 was answered PY because each PEEP strategy was applied for 20 min before outcome measurement and the measured physiology (lung mechanics, drive, EIT) is an acute effect of the prevailing PEEP, the authors cite previous studies that a new steady state is reached within 20 min, and the order-by-strategy interaction showed no carryover (P = 0.932 for ∆PLdyn). The absence of a formal washout period is a limitation, but it does not by itself imply that carryover persisted; any residual carryover would dilute the between-strategy difference rather than create it. The algorithm (S.1 Y/PY and S.3 Y/PY) also gives Low.

D2.rationale: Participants and the staff applying PEEP were not blinded, but no deviations from the assigned intervention occurred: the assigned PEEP was applied for 20 min in every patient, the pressure support level, FiO2 and sedation/analgesia infusions were held constant across all study phases, and all patients completed both steps without interruption. The within-patient paired analysis of both randomised steps estimates the effect of assignment (2.6 Y), so the algorithm (2.3 N, 2.6 Y) and my judgement agree on Low.

D3.rationale: Data for ∆PLdyn were available at both study steps for all 30 randomised patients; the only missing data were central venous oxygen saturation in 4 patients for technical reasons. 3.1 Y, so no further signalling questions apply and the domain is Low.

D4.rationale: The same automated method was used at both steps: ∆PLdyn is calculated from continuously recorded airway and esophageal pressure waveforms, i.e. an objective, software-derived measure with no element of observer judgement. Although the investigators were not blinded, 4.1 N, 4.2 N and 4.4 PN mean the algorithm and my judgement are Low.

D5.rationale: No protocol, statistical analysis plan or registry record is available, so it could not be verified that the analysis of ∆PLdyn was pre-specified before unblinded data were available (5.1 NI). The outcome domain has a single reported measurement (5.2 N) and the analysis described in the Statistical analysis section is the one reported, with the choice between paired t-test and Wilcoxon governed by a normality test rather than by the results (5.3 N), so there is no positive evidence of selective reporting. The algorithm, like my judgement, yields Some concerns because of 5.1 NI.

overall.rationale: All domains are Low except Domain 5, which raises some concerns because pre-specification of the analysis of the primary outcome could not be verified without a protocol, SAP or registry record. No domain is at high risk and the uncertainty in Domain 5 alone does not substantially lower confidence in this physiological result; therefore the study is judged at some concerns overall, in line with the tool's algorithm.
